Store it only in the bot's env file with chmod 600, call only on localhost, and enable API keys only for that user. Choose a single extractor: either the bot runs extraction and Open WebUI's background review stays off, or the reverse. Before adding, dedupe against existing memories with POST /api/v1/memories/query (similarity above about 0.9 means skip). Before relying on the API, check that the GET /api/v1/memories/ response on 0.12 includes the type and path fields. Confirm the thinking-off switch by rendering the Gemma-4 chat template once (look for enable_thinking or the equivalent).

kept.title: Cut per-request prompt overhead in Open WebUI 0.12: Tool Search for big custom tools, a fixed tool list, and pinned Open Terminal settings
kept.what_to_change: Open WebUI 0.12 sends 8 memory tool schemas (add_memory, update_memory, replace_memory_content, delete_memory, search_memories, list_memories, list_memory_paths, read_memory_path) along with SearXNG, fetch, Playwright, deep research, CBU, SQL, screenshot->Excel, Jupyter and terminal tools. Every token of that has to be prefilled on any cache miss. Steps: (1) Enable Admin > Interface > Tool Search (ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true, experimental), TOOL_SEARCH_DEFER_THRESHOLD=400. Set TOOL_SEARCH_ALWAYS_LOADED to the tools used in most turns (for example the search and fetch tool names, plus search_memories). Leave TOOL_SEARCH_DEFER_BUILTIN_TOOLS=true so rarely used memory and notes tools are deferred. (2) Keep the set of tools enabled per model fixed, and never toggle web search or tools mid-chat. (3) For the Open Terminal connection, turn off 'Working Directory Context' and set 'User Shell Tools' to 'Always Include' (new in 0.12, so the tool list does not change when the shell opens or closes).
kept.expected_gain: A smaller and stable prefix. That lowers cold-start TTFT (first message of each chat, or after any cache miss) roughly in proportion to the schema tokens removed, probably 1-4k tokens. It also gives Gemma fewer tools to choose between, which may improve tool choice in Uzbek. The cost is one extra search_tools round trip when a deferred tool is needed.

kept.title: Keep the profile compact and curated: a size budget plus a weekly consolidation pass, instead of growing memory without limit
kept.what_to_change: Set MEMORIES_USER_CHAR_LIMIT=1500 (via /api/v1/configs/import, key memories.user_char_limit; the minimum allowed is 250) so the always-injected block stays at about 400-500 tokens in Uzbek. Organize `user` memories with paths (for example profil/ish, profil/oila, afzallik/javob_uslubi, afzallik/format) so they sort together and read like a profile. Once a week, through Open WebUI Automations or a cron script on the Spark, run a consolidation job at night when the GPU is idle. It should GET /api/v1/memories/, ask Gemma (thinking off) to merge duplicates and remove stale facts into at most 25 one-line facts, and apply the result with POST /api/v1/memories/update. Any memory beyond the character limit is silently cut off at injection, so this matters: the 2000-char default plus slicing means later facts in alphabetical order can disappear without notice.
kept.expected_gain: The most useful facts are always in context, the prefix stays small and stable (it changes once a week instead of mid-day), and no profile facts are silently truncated. Personalization quality goes up with no latency cost.
evidence: v0.12.0 utils/memory.py: '\n\n'.join(user_parts)[:user_limit], a hard character slice after sorting by casefold
docs env-configuration: MEMORIES_USER_CHAR_LIMIT 'Maximum number of characters of user-type memories injected'; persistent config, so set it via configs/import
docs memory.md: memory paths and the update_memory batch operations
kept.applies_to_our_stack: Applies to Open WebUI 0.12 and to the bot via the shared API. Uzbek Latin text uses more tokens than English, so a character budget matters more here.
kept.risk: Low. Consolidation could merge or drop a fact wrongly. Keep a JSON export (GET /api/v1/memories/) before each run so it can be rolled back.
kept.test_plan: Before and after consolidation: measure the length of the rendered memory block (log the system message once) and run a 10-question recall quiz on profile facts. The block should be 1500 chars or less, recall at least as good as before, and there should be 0 duplicate facts.
kept.verifier_reason: The truncation is confirmed: the user block is cut to max(250, memories.user_char_limit), default 2000, after sorting, so later items in sort order drop out silently. A curated, path-organized profile is a good idea. The logic is partly backwards, though. Lowering the limit to 1500 makes silent truncation MORE likely, not less. The guarantee only holds if consolidation keeps the total under the limit, and the job has to check that. 'Open WebUI Automations' as a scheduler is unverified, so a cron script on the Spark is the safer choice. Tokens saved going from 2000 to 1500 chars are tiny, about 150 tokens.
kept.corrected_change: Keep the default 2000 limit, or set 1500 only once the profile is consistently under it. Run a weekly cron script on the Spark at night: export GET /api/v1/memories/ to a dated JSON backup, have Gemma (thinking off, temperature 0) merge the facts into at most 25 path-organized one-line facts, check that the rendered total is under user_char_limit minus a 10% margin (retry or trim if not), then apply with POST /api/v1/memories/update. The same script logs a warning whenever the total user-memory character count exceeds the limit.

kept.title: Use an Uzbek fine-tune instead of stock Whisper large-v3-turbo for STT. Start with the BuzzASR/uzbek benchmark, and use a parakeet-uz model (piyola-v2) as the fast option.
kept.what_to_change: Do not use stock whisper-large-v3-turbo or the Open WebUI built-in faster-whisper for Uzbek. The BuzzASR card reports 28.45% CER for zero-shot large-v3, and turbo is a pruned version of that model with 4 decoder layers instead of 32. Run a 50-100 clip A/B on our own Telegram voice notes with two candidates: (1) BuzzASR/uzbek, a Whisper-large-v3 fine-tune under MIT; load it in fp16 through transformers with num_beams=1, no_repeat_ngram_size=3 and repetition_penalty=1.2, as the card recommends. (2) idrock/piyola-v2 (parakeet-tdt-uz-finetune.nemo), a 617M FastConformer-TDT model under CC-BY-4.0; load it with NeMo EncDecRNNTBPEModel.restore_from and feed it 16 kHz mono audio cut into chunks of 20 s or less. Keep the winner on accuracy as the default. If parakeet comes within about 1-2 points of CER, choose it for its much lower latency. Keep islomov/rubaistt_v2_medium (Whisper-medium, CER about 5.5%, trained with Tashkent-dialect data) as a third candidate if our users speak in dialect.
kept.expected_gain: CER should drop from about 28% (stock large-v3, and turbo is likely worse) to about 3-6%, based on the cards' self-reported FLEURS/CV numbers. On the Omnilingual 'spontaneous' subset, piyola reports 10% CER, which is closer to what real voice notes will look like. This is the single biggest quality improvement for voice input.
evidence: https://huggingface.co/BuzzASR/uzbek: FLEURS CER 6.6 / WER 25.6, CV25 CER 2.68 / WER 11.8, combined CER 3.86 vs 28.45 for zero-shot large-v3. The card claims it beats Omnilingual 1B/7B, MMS and Qwen3-ASR, but gives no numbers for them.
https://huggingface.co/idrock/piyola-v2: FeruzaSpeech CER 1.05%, FLEURS uz CER 2.78% / WER 10.67%, USC CER 3.22%, Omnilingual test CER 10.10%
https://huggingface.co/islomov/rubaistt_v2_medium: WER ~17%, CER ~5.5%
All figures are self-reported on different test sets and normalizations, so they are not directly comparable. I found no independent Uzbek leaderboard.
kept.applies_to_our_stack: Both models fit the memory budget of about 15 GiB free. BuzzASR needs roughly 3-5 GB in fp16 and parakeet roughly 2-5 GB; the dgx-spark-parakeet-asr repo measured about 4.7 GB. Both run on GB10 through the NGC PyTorch container.
kept.risk: Low risk. Self-reported metrics may not hold on noisy phone audio. Whisper fine-tunes can hallucinate on silence, so add VAD trimming. BuzzASR is a full large-v3 model, so it is slower than turbo. Parakeet is CC-BY-4.0, which requires attribution.
kept.test_plan: Collect 100 real Uzbek voice notes from Telegram and hand-correct the transcripts. Compute CER/WER with jiwer after normalizing apostrophes (o' g' and the ʻ variants) and lowercasing. Measure p50/p95 wall-clock time per clip on the Spark while vLLM is under load. Effort: about one day.
kept.verifier_reason: I checked both model cards. BuzzASR/uzbek is a whisper-large-v3 fine-tune under MIT, reporting combined CER 3.86 against 28.45 for zero-shot large-v3, with the recommended settings num_beams=1, no_repeat_ngram_size=3, repetition_penalty=1.2. idrock/piyola-v2 is a 617M FastConformer-TDT fine-tuned from parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2 under CC-BY-4.0, trained on 0.1-20 s clips, and its reported CERs match the recommendation. Both fit the memory budget easily. Three caveats. First, the piyola card's usage code loads the repo id 'idrock/parakeet-tdt-uz-finetune', not 'idrock/piyola-v2', so pin whichever id actually contains the .nemo file. Second, FeruzaSpeech and USC may overlap the training data, so its low CER on those sets is suspect; trust only our own clips. Third, to save memory, keep just one winner loaded in production, not both.
kept.corrected_change: Same A/B test. Download parakeet-tdt-uz-finetune.nemo with hf_hub_download, checking which repo id (idrock/piyola-v2 or idrock/parakeet-tdt-uz-finetune) actually holds the file, and load it with EncDecRNNTBPEModel.restore_from. Base the decision only on our own 100 Telegram clips, not on card numbers, because FeruzaSpeech and USC may be in-domain for training. Deploy only the winner; do not keep both resident.

kept.title: Run STT as one OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/transcriptions service in an NGC container on GB10, and do not use the faster-whisper or speaches arm64 images.
kept.what_to_change: Base the container on nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:25.11-py3 or newer; NGC 25.03+ has sm_121, while 24.x does not. Add a small FastAPI wrapper that exposes POST /v1/audio/transcriptions (multipart file, model, language, response_format) and runs the model chosen in recommendation 1. The repo github.com/mARTin-B78/dgx-spark-parakeet-asr already does this for parakeet on port 8010 and can be forked: set its model loading to the Uzbek .nemo file. Inside the service, run 'ffmpeg -i in -ar 16000 -ac 1 -f wav -' on every input, add VAD (silero) and keep the model loaded at all times. Avoid ghcr.io/speaches-ai/speaches:latest-cuda: its arm64 ctranslate2 is a CPU-only build (issue #620, still open), and in CPU mode a commenter reported 40-100 s to transcribe 20 s of audio. If we specifically want Whisper speed, one alternative is whisper.cpp built with -DGGML_CUDA=1 -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=121, with BuzzASR converted through models/convert-h5-to-ggml.py. Converting a fine-tune this way is untested by me.
kept.expected_gain: A single local endpoint that both Open WebUI and the Telegram bot can call, which avoids loading the model twice and wasting memory. The parakeet reference on DGX Spark reports about 15x real-time, so a 10 s voice note should take well under 1 s. I found no published GB10 latency for Whisper-large fine-tunes, and we need to measure it.
evidence: https://github.com/speaches-ai/speaches/issues/620: arm64 image ships CPU-only CTranslate2; NGC 24.x lacks sm_121 and 25.03+ has it
https://github.com/mARTin-B78/dgx-spark-parakeet-asr: NGC pytorch 25.11 base, ~15x RTF, ~4.7 GB GPU mem, 60-90 s cold load, OpenAI-compatible endpoint

https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/dgx-spark-vibevoice-tts-streaming-voice-pipeline-setup-guide/356424: whisper.cpp large-v3-turbo runs on Spark, ~766 ms to first audio end to end (not broken down by stage)
https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/building-llama-cpp-container-images-for-spark-gb10/353664: ggml CUDA Docker builds need the CUDA 13 compat LD_LIBRARY_PATH fix
kept.applies_to_our_stack: This runs alongside vLLM 0.31 on the same GPU. Put a low priority on the service and keep it permanently loaded; the 60-90 s cold start rules out lazy loading. Memory cost is about 5 GB of our 15 GiB headroom.
kept.risk: Medium risk. NeMo or transformers dependency friction on aarch64. STT and LLM decode compete for the same 273 GB/s memory bandwidth, so STT will briefly slow token generation. The NGC image is about 15 GB to download, which takes roughly 30-50 minutes at 5-8 MB/s.
kept.test_plan: Run curl -F file=@note.ogg -F model=uz http://localhost:8010/v1/audio/transcriptions. Then measure LLM tok/s with and without 4 concurrent transcriptions, and check nvidia-smi / free -g for memory headroom. Effort: 0.5-1 day.
kept.verifier_reason: Verified. speaches issue #620 is open: the arm64 latest-cuda image ships a CPU-only CTranslate2, and a commenter reported 40-100 s for 20 s of audio. In the same thread, a GB10 user running openai-whisper large-v3 in NGC 25.03 got about 9.5x real time on the GPU. kept.title: Telegram bot: handle voice notes as Opus in, send STT text to the existing agent loop, and send Opus voice back. Pipeline it so the user sees text first.
